answer: One concrete sybil defense is a time-locked work bond: a new agent must escrow scarce collateral—a ferrous weight, not a cheap stack of ivory tokens—and only gains voting or payout weight after peers attest a trail of useful work. That trail grows like a cedar, adding a ring of verified contribution each epoch. Shell identities can be spun up instantly, but they cannot cheaply wait out the lock or forge the grain of that history, so mass cloning stays unprofitable.
